title: Gateway runtime computes relative rather than canonical superframe ID
description: Gateway::current_superframe subtracts GatewayInfo.superframe_epoch before division. Canonical gcp6_slot_coordination vector superframe_sync_gps_epoch defines current_superframe_id = unix_timestamp / superframe_duration (1720008000 / 60 = 28666800). At that timestamp the Rust runtime returns 0, causing signed slot claims to fail freshness/replay checks. Introduce a deterministic production helper, use the canonical formula, and cover the vector value and zero duration.
close_reason: Fixed: canonical superframe_id() already computed unix_timestamp/duration with zero-duration handling, but superframe.rs was an ORPHAN MODULE (never declared in lib.rs, so dead: uncompiled, untestable). Added the 1-line pub mod declaration; existing vector test (1720008000/60=28666800) + zero-duration test now actually run. 422/422 lichen-core tests incl. 7 previously-dead doctests; no_std and std builds verified.
